title: anomaly-labeling-and-feedback-loop-guidelines-2025
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This document describes a standardized process for labeling anomalies detected across Redwood inference systems and closing the loop with automated and human-in-the-loop feedback. The goal is to: 1) make anomaly signals actionable, 2) ensure consistent triage, 3) route corrective actions to the right owners, and 4) feed labels back into detectors and model-quality evaluations.

Motivation:

We operate heterogeneous detection sources (statistical detectors, model-eval alerts, user-reported incidents). Without consistent labels and a unified feedback flow, detectors become noisy, teams re-triage the same issues, and model-quality regressions go unaddressed. This guideline prescribes taxonomy, minimum metadata, routing, and an automated feedback loop to retrain detectors and surface regression windows to model-evals.

Scope:

- Applies to anomalies from production inference pipelines, telemetry pipeline (anomaly-farm-service), model-eval alerts, and synthetic-sensor tests.
- Covers the lifecycle from initial detection to final disposition and label propagation into detectors/evals.
- Excludes: purely infra-level hardware failures with existing SRE runbooks (see eng-sre/runbooks).

Key definitions:

- anomaly: an observable deviation from baseline telemetry (latency, token-error-rate, response-quality, semantic drift).
- label: canonical tag assigned to an anomaly for classification (see taxonomy).
- triage: human or automated decision that assigns root cause, priority, and action owner.
- feedback loop: automated propagation of final labels to (a) detector training sets, (b) model-eval history, and (c) routing/feature-flag triggers.

Signal taxonomy (required labels):

1) severity:[sev1|sev2|sev3] — maps to SLO impact.
2) category:[latency|cost-spike|quality-drift|config-regression|infrastructure|telemetry-gap|false-positive].
3) subcategory — free-form short token list (e.g., kv-cache-eviction, batch-surge, quantization-glitch).
4) root_cause_hint — one-word hint (e.g., kernel, packing, routing, model-version).
5) actionable:[yes|no] — whether immediate remediation is recommended.
6) reviewer_notes — short text summary (10–40 words).

Minimum metadata schema (every labeled anomaly):

| field | format | example | required? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | uuid | 3f9b2c28-1a3f-4d6f-aa3b-1234abcd0001 | yes |
| detected_at | RFC3339 | 2025-01-14T15:02:11Z | yes |
| source | string | anomaly-farm-service | yes |
| metric | string | request_latency_p99 | yes |
| window_start/window_end | RFC3339 | 2025-01-14T14:55:00Z / 2025-01-14T15:00:00Z | yes |
| labels | list of tags | ["sev2","latency","kv-cache-eviction"] | yes |
| owner | team shorthand | eng-serving-runtime | yes |
| disposition | string | triaged/ignored/mitigated/monitor-only | yes |

Labeling process and ownership:

1) automated classification: detectors attach preliminary labels using heuristics and model-based classifiers (service: anomaly-farm-classifier). Preliminary labels must include severity and category.
2) routing: anomalies with severity sev1 or actionable=yes are routed to on-call Slack channel (#oncall-sev1) and create PagerDuty incidents per SRE routing rules.
3) human triage: triagers validate labels within 30 minutes for sev1, 4 hours for sev2, 72 hours for sev3. Triagers update root_cause_hint, subcategory, and disposition.
4) ownership assignment: triage assigns an owner team. If ownership is ambiguous, assign to eng-platform for cross-service arbitration.

Automated vs human review rules:

- Automated-only if: detector confidence >= 0.98 AND category in [telemetry-gap,false-positive]. Must still be batched for weekly sample review.
- Human-required if: severity == sev1 OR metric in [semantic_quality_nce, hallucination_rate] OR detector confidence < 0.7.

Feedback loop and propagation actions:

- When disposition == mitigated or triaged with root cause confirmed, an automated job (feedback-propagator) runs to:
  - push labeled examples to detector-training-bucket (tagged by detector version),
  - append the event to model-eval windows with label metadata,
  - create a changelog entry for feature-flag or release lockdown if remediation involved rollbacks.
- If disposition == ignored, the event is retained for 30 days and sampled into a false-positive audit set.

Metric SLOs and KPIs for the feedback loop:

- triage-latency: 30m (sev1), 4h (sev2), 72h (sev3). Target: 90th percentile under SLO.
- label-consensus: percent of anomalies where automated label matches final human label. Target: >80% for latency and infra categories within 90 days of deployment.
- feedback-ingest-completeness: fraction of confirmed anomalies successfully written to detector-training-bucket. Target: 99.5%.

Privacy and retention:

- Anomaly records may contain prompt or user-provided content only when required for root cause. Such records must be redacted per data-management guidelines and marked confidentiality:restricted.
- Retention: labeled anomalies retained for 1 year; false-positive audit set retained 90 days.

Operational runbook (short):

1) Incident detected: check auto-labels in telemetry UI and open triage page.
2) Validate basic metadata (id, window, metric). If missing, tag as telemetry-gap and file infra ticket.
3) For sev1: escalate via PagerDuty and post a summary to #oncall-sev1 with the label payload.
4) For model-quality categories: capture 3 representative examples (anonymize PII), attach to model-eval ticket, and notify applied-ml-and-evals.
5) After mitigation: mark disposition and set owner actions (hotfix, rollback, model-retrain).

Implementation checklist (minimum viable rollout):

- [ ] Implement label schema in anomaly event envelope (anomaly-farm-service v2).
- [ ] Add a triage UI view with quick-label and owner-assign actions.
- [ ] Wire feedback-propagator job with retries and idempotency keys.
- [ ] Create weekly false-positive audit workflow and reviewer rotation.
- [ ] Define Slack and PagerDuty routing rules for sev1 and sev2.

Example payload (in plain JSON, stored in event-store):

{
  "id": "3f9b2c28-1a3f-4d6f-aa3b-1234abcd0001",
  "detected_at": "2025-01-14T15:02:11Z",
  "source": "anomaly-farm-service",
  "metric": "response_semantic_similarity_drop",
  "window_start": "2025-01-14T14:55:00Z",
  "window_end": "2025-01-14T15:00:00Z",
  "labels": ["sev2","quality-drift","model-version"],
  "owner": "applied-ml-and-evals",
  "disposition": "triaged",
  "reviewer_notes": "sudden similarity drop after model v3.1 rollback recommended"
}

CLI triage snippet (example):

# list untriaged anomalies
redwood-observe anomalies list --status untriaged --limit 50

# assign an owner and add labels
redwood-observe anomalies annotate --id 3f9b2c28 --labels sev2,quality-drift --owner applied-ml-and-evals --note "Investigate model bundle v3.1"

Quality guardrails and experimental cadence:

- Re-evaluate detector heuristics quarterly and measure label-consensus KPI.
- For new detectors, run a 30-day shadow labeling period where human labels are collected but not used for automatic routing. If consensus > 75% and precision meets target, enable automated routing.

Ownership and escalation matrix:

- primary owners: eng-serving-runtime (latency, kv-cache, batching), applied-ml-and-evals (quality-drift, hallucinations), eng-infra (GPU/thermal).
- cross-team arbitration: eng-platform.
- SRE escalation: if sev1 persists > 60 minutes with no mitigation, SRE lead escalates to VP Eng.

- detector training bucket: s3://redwood-anomaly-training/
